review_notes: The official eVisa nationality table explicitly lists Bangladesh (BD/BGD) as Visa Required. The current Government of Anguilla page states that holders of a UK visa do not need a separate Anguilla visa; it also lists US$140 single-entry and US$250 multiple-entry fees, an online eVisa route, and an 8–10 business-day processing estimate. The page also directs visa applicants to the nearest British Embassy or High Commission. A 2017 Government press release additionally mentioned valid US/Canada visas or residence permits, but the current page omits those exceptions; do not rely on the older US/Canada exception without written confirmation. official_immigration_source_name: NetherlandsWorldwide — Caribbean visa nationality exemptions and conditions
review_notes: Bangladesh is not included in the official nationality-based visa-exempt list. A Bangladeshi ordinary passport holder therefore needs a short-stay Caribbean visa unless a separate exemption applies: a multiple-entry Schengen visa or Schengen residence permit; a multiple-entry UK or Ireland visa or residence permit; or a US/Canada residence card. The US/Canada multiple-entry-visa exemption is limited to named nationalities and Bangladesh is not listed. One short-stay Caribbean visa covers Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, St Eustatius and Sint Maarten; it is not valid for European Netherlands or Schengen. The short-stay visa permits up to 90 days within 180 days, subject to each island's own maximum. Paid work is not permitted. The official tourism checklist states that VFS Global captures a digital photo at the appointment; a separate printed photo is not required through VFS.
